decision.rationale: Audited seed-42 development mean HR@10 was 0.5795 for the candidate, 0.575 for the generated control, and 0.59475 for the incumbent. Both new arms fell below the incumbent and were ineligible for confirmation. The candidate exceeded the control by 0.0045, but its result was below the proposal’s 0.59975 threshold and below the incumbent in every category. The predicted gain for users with 1–5 training interactions was negative in all four categories. The development comparison does not establish a causal mechanism; no confirmation result was supplied.
unresolved_explanations: The candidate–control contrast was mixed by category, including a 0.019 HR@10 loss for the candidate in Industrial_and_Scientific. Count direction, overall context attenuation, and category effects remain competing explanations.
Independent training trajectories and public-validation checkpoint selection may explain the small candidate–control mean difference.
Several history slices had null effects; sparse long-history bins and the absence of generated-control history-bin results prevent a discriminating history interaction test.

The author could not run CPU checks locally. Host admission and pre/post training synthetic contracts report success, but those finite checks do not prove the proposed mechanism or all-input behavior. Direct numerical equivalence of forward and candidate-scoring states before and after training was not supplied.
No independent-seed replication, held-out confirmation, or average-context-matched fixed-weight control was supplied.
